artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia (Pompeii fresco)
artworks.description: A Fourth Style fresco from Pompeii (Naples, MAN inv. 9112) stages the Aulis sacrifice: Iphigenia carried toward the altar while Agamemnon turns away and Artemis prepares the deer that will take her place. The wall-painting preserves the Euripidean hinge of the Trojan War — the daughter whose blood buys the winds for Troy. Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Naples.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Tiepolo's airy Venetian oil fills the altar with priests, soldiers, and the pale princess at the centre of the rite. Iphigenia is the price Agamemnon pays so the fleet can sail — the sacrifice that Clytemnestra will never forgive. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: Pylades and Orestes Brought as Victims before Iphigenia
artworks.description: West's National Gallery canvas turns to Iphigenia in Tauris: the priestess of Artemis faces the two Greek strangers she must sacrifice, not yet knowing one is her brother Orestes. The painting freezes Euripides' recognition drama — the sister Artemis saved at Aulis, now almost the instrument of a second family blood-debt. Oil on canvas, National Gallery, London.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Doyen's French baroque composition crowds the Aulis shore with the stalled fleet, the altar, and Iphigenia as the chosen victim. The canvas makes visible the war's first cost: a princess offered so Helen's husband and his brother can sail. Oil on canvas.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Steen's Dutch history painting stages the altar at Aulis with the princess, the knife, and the watching army. Iphigenia appears as the tragic hinge between household and war — the daughter whose death (or divine rescue) opens the road to Troy. Oil on canvas.

films.title: Iphigenia
films.description: Cacoyannis' Euripides film is the Aulis sacrifice itself: Iphigenia walking toward the altar so the fleet can sail for Troy.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: The USA Network miniseries keeps the Aulis episode in view — Iphigenia as the price Agamemnon pays before Helen's war begins.

music.title: Iphigénie en Aulide
music.description: Gluck's first Iphigenia opera is the sacrifice at Aulis: the daughter, the stalled winds, and the father who must choose the war.

music.title: Iphigénie en Tauride
music.description: The sequel finds Iphigenia alive as priestess in Tauris — the sister who almost sacrifices the brother she does not yet know.

music.title: Iphigénie en Tauride
music.description: Piccinni's rival Tauris opera keeps Iphigenia as Artemis's priestess — the sister who must choose between Greek strangers and the goddess's altar.

popCulture.title: Iphigenia in Aulis
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' Aulis play is the sacrifice itself — Iphigenia walking to the altar so the fleet can sail for Troy.

popCulture.title: Iphigenia in Tauris
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: The sequel finds Iphigenia alive in Tauris as priestess — almost the instrument of her brother Orestes' death before recognition saves them.

popCulture.title: Iphigenia in Tauris
popCulture.creator: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
popCulture.description: Goethe's verse drama humanizes the Tauris priestess — Iphigenia as Enlightenment conscience who will not sacrifice the strangers.

popCulture.title: The Songs of the Kings
popCulture.creator: Barry Unsworth
popCulture.description: Unsworth retells the Aulis crisis as modern spin and scapegoating — Iphigenia still the price the kings demand before Troy.
